title: The Rights of Non-Muslims under Islamic Law
subtitle: The Quranic foundations of religious protection, the dhimma system, and equal citizenship today
summary: Islam makes justice toward non-Muslims and faithfulness to their protection matters of accountability before God. Quran 60:8 commands kindness and justice, and authentic hadith warn against killing or wronging a covenant partner. Premodern protected status also contained real inequalities; modern equal-citizenship approaches are developments argued from Islamic principles, not an exact description of all historical law.

seo.metaTitle: Rights of Non-Muslims under Islamic Law: Dhimma, Jizya, and the Modern Debate
seo.metaDescription: The Quran and authentic Sunnah protect peaceful non-Muslims, their lives, property, worship, and covenants, while commanding justice and kindness.

sections.title: Another Person's Safety Is Not Conditional on Conversion
sections.body:
Quran 60:8 commands kindness and justice toward those not fighting Muslims or expelling them. Quran 5:8 requires justice even when hostility makes it hard. These duties give Muslims a positive reason to protect a non-Muslim neighbor, not merely tolerate someone useful.

Islam also claims to be true and invites people to it. Invitation and civil protection are different questions: disagreement about salvation does not permit betrayal, theft, or murder.

sections.title: A Wronged Non-Muslim Can Have a Claim Against a Muslim Before God
sections.body:
[Sahih al-Bukhari 3166](https://sunnah.com/bukhari:3166) gives a severe warning against killing a person under covenant. [Sunan Abi Dawud 3052](https://sunnah.com/abudawud:3052), graded sound by al-Albani, warns against wronging a covenant partner, diminishing rights, overburdening him, or taking property without consent.

The moral force is not merely that a state prefers order. The offender answers to God, and the Prophet is described as pleading for the wronged person on Judgment Day. Religious difference does not put someone's rights outside a Muslim's accountability.

sections.title: Religious Community in Medina
sections.body:
The Constitution of Medina placed Muslims and Jewish clans in one political order. It recognized distinct religions and mutual duties. Historians debate its exact date and compilation, but many see early material in it. Later conflicts with particular tribes need their political and military context. They do not erase the principle that a non-Muslim community could belong without conversion.

The charter is not a modern constitution. It shows that the Prophet's community included religious groups under shared defense and law. The Quran also commands good debate with the People of the Book, except against injustice (29:46). Theology and civil wrongdoing remain distinct.

sections.title: The Hard Objection: Protection With Unequal Status
sections.body:
Dhimma was a premodern covenant protecting recognized non-Muslim communities within Muslim rule. Jizya, addressed in Quran 9:29, was part of that status system; Muslims had zakat and their own duties. Eligibility, exemptions, rates, and enforcement varied across law and practice.

It was not simply a modern protection tax under equal citizenship. The framework could include restrictions and legal inequalities, and jizya also marked political submission. Those features cannot be erased by saying minorities were protected, just as protection cannot be erased by saying the status was unequal.

The Islamic defense must explain both the historical arrangement and its purpose of stable coexistence without requiring everyone to convert. It must also confront how justice and covenant should be fulfilled under a different modern political order.

sections.title: Survival Is Evidence of Space for Difference, Not Proof of Perfect Justice
sections.body:
Jewish, Christian, and other communities preserved religious life for long periods under Muslim rule. That record contradicts the idea that conversion or extermination was the only possible outcome. It does not establish that every period was tolerant or every restriction just.

Historical wrongdoing needs specific study rather than a contest between idealized civilizations. Islam's norms are most credible when they are used to confront Muslim persecution as well as to recognize genuine protection.

sections.title: Equal Citizenship Is an Islamic Argument, Not a False Historical Claim
sections.body:
A contemporary Muslim case for equal citizenship applies justice, shared civic obligations, and fidelity to covenant to present political conditions. Egypt's [Dar al-Ifta reports its Grand Mufti affirming equal rights and duties for Egyptian citizens](https://www.dar-alifta.org/en/article/details/715/the-grand-mufti-of-egypt-meets-with-the-foreign-relations-committee-in-the-dutch). This is a real institutional position, not a claim that every classical jurist already taught modern citizenship.

Scholars differ over the relationship between such arrangements and older status rules. Theological disagreement remains even where civil protection is equal. A Muslim can believe Islam true without treating a fellow citizen's safety as negotiable.

sections.title: Make Your Neighbor's Trust Part of Your Worship
sections.body:
Islam asks a Muslim to be trustworthy when the other person does not share his faith. The Quranic command to justice and the Prophetic warning against wronging a covenant partner make that duty spiritually serious.

For a seeker, this is an invitation to a faith that places rights above in-group convenience, not a denial of its difficult legal history. Read [Human Dignity and Justice](/articles/human-dignity-and-justice) next. If the question is specifically freedom to leave Islam, continue to [Punishment for Apostasy and War](/articles/punishment-for-apostasy-and-war), where the disagreement is treated directly.

quranVerses.arabic: لَّا يَنْهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ لَمْ يُقَٰتِلُوكُمْ فِى ٱلدِّينِ وَلَمْ يُخْرِجُوكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمْ أَن تَبَرُّوهُمْ وَتُقْسِطُوٓا۟ إِلَيْهِمْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُقْسِطِينَ
quranVerses.translation: Allah does not forbid you from those who do not fight you because of religion and do not expel you from your homes - from being righteous toward them and acting justly toward them. Indeed, Allah loves those who act justly.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: إِنَّمَا يَنْهَىٰكُمُ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلَّذِينَ قَٰتَلُوكُمْ فِى ٱلدِّينِ وَأَخْرَجُوكُم مِّن دِيَٰرِكُمْ وَظَٰهَرُوا۟ عَلَىٰٓ إِخْرَاجِكُمْ أَن تَوَلَّوْهُمْ ۚ وَمَن يَتَوَلَّهُمْ فَأُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ
quranVerses.translation: Allah only forbids you from those who fight you because of religion and expel you from your homes and aid in your expulsion - [forbids] that you make allies of them. And whoever makes allies of them, then it is those who are the wrongdoers.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: لَآ إِكْرَاهَ فِى ٱلدِّينِ ۖ قَد تَّبَيَّنَ ٱلرُّشْدُ مِنَ ٱلْغَىِّ ۚ فَمَن يَكْفُرْ بِٱلطَّٰغُوتِ وَيُؤْمِنۢ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدِ ٱسْتَمْسَكَ بِٱلْعُرْوَةِ ٱلْوُثْقَىٰ لَا ٱنفِصَامَ لَهَا ۗ وَٱللَّهُ سَمِيعٌ عَلِيمٌ
quranVerses.translation: There shall be no compulsion in [acceptance of] the religion. The right course has become clear from the wrong. So whoever disbelieves in Taghut and believes in Allah has grasped the most trustworthy handhold with no break in it. And Allah is Hearing and Knowing.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: ٱلَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا۟ مِن دِيَٰرِهِم بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّآ أَن يَقُولُوا۟ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ۗ وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍۢ لَّهُدِّمَتْ صَوَٰمِعُ وَبِيَعٌۭ وَصَلَوَٰتٌۭ وَمَسَٰجِدُ يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ كَثِيرًۭا ۗ وَلَيَنصُرَنَّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَنصُرُهُۥٓ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌ
quranVerses.translation: [They are] those who have been evicted from their homes without right - only because they say, "Our Lord is Allah." And were it not that Allah checks the people, some by means of others, there would have been demolished monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned. And Allah will surely support those who support Him. Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: قَٰتِلُوا۟ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَلَا بِٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ وَلَا يُحَرِّمُونَ مَا حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥ وَلَا يَدِينُونَ دِينَ ٱلْحَقِّ مِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوا۟ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ حَتَّىٰ يُعْطُوا۟ ٱلْجِزْيَةَ عَن يَدٍۢ وَهُمْ صَٰغِرُونَ
quranVerses.translation: Fight those who do not believe in Allah or in the Last Day and who do not consider unlawful what Allah and His Messenger have made unlawful and who do not adopt the religion of truth from those who were given the Scripture - [fight] until they give the jizyah willingly while they are humbled.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُونُوا۟ قَوَّٰمِينَ لِلَّهِ شُهَدَآءَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ ۖ وَلَا يَجْرِمَنَّكُمْ شَنَـَٔانُ قَوْمٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَلَّا تَعْدِلُوا۟ ۚ ٱعْدِلُوا۟ هُوَ أَقْرَبُ لِلتَّقْوَىٰ ۖ وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ خَبِيرٌۢ بِمَا تَعْمَلُونَ
quranVerses.translation: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice, and do not let the hatred of a people prevent you from being just. Be just; that is nearer to righteousness. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

quranVerses.arabic: ۞ وَلَا تُجَٰدِلُوٓا۟ أَهْلَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ إِلَّا بِٱلَّتِى هِىَ أَحْسَنُ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ مِنْهُمْ ۖ وَقُولُوٓا۟ ءَامَنَّا بِٱلَّذِىٓ أُنزِلَ إِلَيْنَا وَأُنزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ وَإِلَٰهُنَا وَإِلَٰهُكُمْ وَٰحِدٌۭ وَنَحْنُ لَهُۥ مُسْلِمُونَ
quranVerses.translation: And do not argue with the People of the Scripture except in a way that is best, except for those who commit injustice among them, and say, "We believe in that which has been revealed to us and revealed to you. And our God and your God is one; and we are Muslims [in submission] to Him."
quranVerses.sourceAttribution: api.alquran.cloud — Tanzil Uthmani text; Saheeh International translation

bibleVerses.text: “‘If a stranger lives as a foreigner with you in your land, you shall not do him wrong. The stranger who lives as a foreigner with you shall be to you as the native-born among you, and you shall love him as yourself; for you lived as foreigners in the land of Egypt. I am Yahweh your God.
“You shall not wrong an alien or oppress him, for you were aliens in the land of Egypt.

faq.question: Does the Quran command kindness toward non-Muslims?
faq.answer: Yes. Quran 60:8 commands kindness and justice toward those who do not fight or expel Muslims, and 5:8 commands justice even toward people one dislikes.

faq.question: What does Islam say about killing a protected non-Muslim?
faq.answer: Sahih al-Bukhari 3166 warns that the killer of a person under covenant will not smell the fragrance of Paradise.

faq.question: Was dhimma equal citizenship?
faq.answer: No. Dhimma was a premodern covenant with substantial protections and real inequalities. Contemporary equal-citizenship approaches are argued from justice, covenant, and changed political conditions; they are not an exact restatement of every older status rule.

faq.question: Is the Covenant of St. Catherine reliable evidence?
faq.answer: Its received form is historically disputed, so it should not carry the argument. The Quran and rigorously authenticated hadith already establish protection without relying on that document.

furtherReading.title: Under Crescent and Cross: The Jews in the Middle Ages
furtherReading.author: Mark R. Cohen
furtherReading.note: The standard comparative study of Jewish life under medieval Islam and Christendom; explicitly answers both the 'interfaith utopia' myth and the 'perpetual persecution' countermyth. Princeton University Press, 1994.

furtherReading.title: Tolerance and Coercion in Islam: Interfaith Relations in the Muslim Tradition
furtherReading.author: Yohanan Friedmann
furtherReading.note: A rigorous study of how classical jurists actually reasoned about non-Muslims, apostasy, and religious hierarchy, built on close reading of the legal sources. Cambridge University Press, 2003.

furtherReading.title: Non-Muslims in the Early Islamic Empire: From Surrender to Coexistence
furtherReading.author: Milka Levy-Rubin
furtherReading.note: Traces the surrender agreements and the Pact of Umar's provisions to Byzantine and Sasanian precedents, showing how the dhimma rules crystallized historically. Cambridge University Press, 2011.

furtherReading.title: Religious Pluralism and Islamic Law: Dhimmis and Others in the Empire of Law
furtherReading.author: Anver M. Emon
furtherReading.note: A legal-theoretical analysis arguing the dhimma rules are best understood as governance of diversity within an imperial legal order — neither simple tolerance nor simple persecution. Oxford University Press, 2012.
